client.name: Hearthline
client.cause: Ending fuel poverty for older people in the UK

exampleLines: Nobody should have to choose between heating and eating.
A warm home is not a luxury.

proofPoints: Last winter Hearthline helped 4,200 older people stay warm
£30 covers a week of heating for one household
£75 pays for an emergency boiler repair callout
£150 funds a home energy visit and insulation kit
92% of the people we helped said they felt less anxious about bills
Hearthline has worked in local communities since 2009
complianceNotes: Never show real service users' faces without written consent
Gift Aid statement must appear on every donation page
Avoid implying 100% of donations go to direct services

audience.name: Warm-hearted 45-65s
audience.description: UK adults aged 45-65 with ageing parents, who already give to at least one charity and worry about older relatives in winter
motivations: Wants to protect older people like their own parents
Likes to see exactly what a gift pays for
objections: Worried the money goes on admin
Assumes the government covers heating support

offer.ask: Help an older person stay warm this winter

donationTiers.impact: covers a week of heating for one household
pays for an emergency boiler repair callout
funds a home energy visit and insulation kit

offer.matchFunding: Every gift doubled by the Ashby Foundation until 31 January

keyMessage: This winter, a warm home for an older person costs less than you think, and right now your gift goes twice as far.

creativeContext.problemInDailyLife: Older people heat one room and tell nobody.
creativeContext.storySeed: My nan heated one room last winter and told nobody.
creativeContext.openingQuestion: When did you last check how warm your mum's house is?
creativeContext.whatWeDo: finds them, fixes the immediate problem and helps them claim the support they are entitled to.
creativeContext.caseStudy: Last winter a retired postman in Leeds was heating his kitchen with the oven door open. A Hearthline home visit fixed his boiler timer, fitted draught excluders and sorted a grant he did not know existed. He told the team he had stopped dreading the postman. Names and details changed to protect privacy; the case is real.

references: Previous winter appeal: best performing creative was a stat-led static with a single older person's hands around a mug
